page: Amazon Web Services m5a.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with an AMD EPYC 7571 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 8 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, depending entirely on network-attached storage, and does not feature GPU accelerators. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reflects the capabilities of the first-generation AMD EPYC platform. Single-core evaluation via stress-ng registers at 591.0, while Geekbench single-core reaches 729.0, both settling in the lower decile of tested architectures. Multi-threaded performance scales to 2360.94 in stress-ng and 2960.0 in Geekbench. PassMark metrics indicate moderate CPU compute performance at 6871.6 and encryption capabilities of 6484.1, enabled by native AES and SHA-NI hardware instruction sets. Memory bandwidth tests yield 310.05 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 27.54 GB/sec for large uncached reads, supporting Redis throughput of roughly 4.98 million operations per second alongside 5.01 GB/sec of static web serving bandwidth.

The m5a.2xlarge is structured for standard production workloads where memory capacity is prioritized over top-tier single-thread instruction throughput. By utilizing first-generation AMD EPYC silicon, it offers resource density at a favorable hardware cost profile compared to higher-clocked compute-optimized families. However, applications requiring extensive vector extensions will encounter limitations due to lack of AVX-512 support. The absence of local NVMe storage also shifts all I/O dependency to network volumes. Given these architectural trade-offs, the server is suitable for medium-scale web application hosting, backend microservices, caching layers, and asynchronous batch worker processing.
description: Amazon Web Services m5a.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32 GB of DDR4 system memory running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz across 4 physical cores and 8 threads, backed by 8 MB of L3 cache per core. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the hardware configuration provides 4.0 GB of RAM per core alongside baseline networking performance of 2 Gbps. It features no local ephemeral storage, requiring remote storage volumes, and contains no hardware GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place its single-core and multi-core raw compute capabilities in lower-tier brackets, while cryptographic and baseline memory metrics show moderate throughput. Because of its steady memory allocation and conservative per-core processing output, the m5a.2xlarge functions best for mid-tier web serving, standard business applications, staging environments, and distributed background batch tasks.
